articles.title: Emerald Crown
articles.summary: Green, lime and yellow wavy vertical bands, broad soft grain, satin sheen with sparkle. A green-to-yellow gradient with a sparkly metallic feel; dark emerald at the top, gold at the bottom, reads as a candy-flake fade.
articles.what: Emerald Crown gradient blend Up close: A smooth top-to-bottom fade from dark forest green through emerald and bright lime into golden yellow, covered in a fine, even glitter grain with a few brighter lime sparkle dots. No stripes or bands; the colour only changes with height. From a distance: A green-to-yellow gradient with a sparkly metallic feel; dark emerald at the top, gold at the bottom, reads as a candy-flake fade. Measured spec (average): metal 117, roughness 116, coat 123. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, sides.
Fits: gt / sports car, stock car, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Emerald Crown" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Sides and doors: the fade runs top to bottom, dark at the roof, gold at the rocker
Hood is fine; the fade stretches over the car
White or black numbers read; green or yellow numbers vanish in matching zones of the fade.
Bold white or black graphics, stripes: sit well over a smooth fade
Pairs well with: white, chrome, black, gold.
pitfalls: Not wavy vertical bands: it is a smooth vertical fade (the old card is wrong)
Not a flat colour: five colour stops from dark to gold
Avoid: green numbers on green bands, next to other loud gradients.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 117 (pearl-level metal), roughness 116 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 123 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: green numbers on green bands, next to other loud gradients.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold white or black graphics, stripes: sit well over a smooth fade; a thin chrome pinline: fits

Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
